attributes.evidence: MEASURED INSIDE ONE FUNCTION, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. fn_800C03E0 has THREE trailer loops of identical source shape (`j = qline - 20; for (k = 0, i = 0; k < N; k++, i += S)`) using the same function-scope `i` and `k`. At head 1370dce50 the mode==3 trailer (k<3) already matched the target byte-for-byte -- `fnasm 0x1a8:0x1e4 --diff` shows ours emitting `addi r17,r30,-20 / li r20,0 / li r19,0 / lis r18,256` against the target's `addi r19,r31,-20 / li r20,0 / li r16,0 / lis r17,256`, same order, two independent li -- while the mode==2 and mode==4 trailers emitted `li r16,0 / addi r19,r16,0 / addi r20,r30,-20 / lis r18,256`, a CSEd copy with the j computation pushed to third. Same source shape, same statement order, opposite codegen: source order is therefore excluded as the discriminant before any build. Converting ONLY the mode==2 trailer to block-scope `tk`/`ti` closed its cluster (real 514 -> 512, multiset 4t -> IDENTICAL 433/433, fuzzy 95.9931 -> 96.3857) and converting the mode==4 trailer the same way closed the second (real 512 -> 508, fuzzy 96.3857 -> 96.7783, clusters 3 -> 1). The mode==3 control was held on the function-scope form throughout and stayed byte-identical, so the conversion is not a global perturbation. THE REFUTED ALTERNATIVE: attempt.NC_fn800c03e0-a-missing-textx-local-and-a-spurious-row-pointer-copy.20260903.v1 recorded a mandated step-1 hypothesis saying to attack the EMISSION ORDER first and explicitly NOT to try to break the zero CSE, on the reasoning that the same copy-vs-li choice appears in the opposite direction elsewhere in the function. The order lever was measured NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL and breaking the CSE is what worked.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 (n=30, established) SCREENED and NARROWED, not overturned: that law's evidence is that no SPELLING of the zero moves the decision, and every spelling probe in this session agreed with it (three NEUTRAL-IDENTICALs). What this law adds is that the allocator's input -- web membership -- is itself a source-level choice, so 'allocator not source' is true of the zero and false of the variable that carries it. claim.law.dead-local-identity-reuse-flips-callee-saved-coloring.20260831.v1 is the nearest prior and predicted the direction. claim.LZ_copy-form-taxonomy-and-payoff-inversion.20260901.v1 SCREENED as the copy-form taxonomy this row belongs to.
attributes.scope: MWCC 1.2.5n at the -O4 no-peephole demo cflags used by game/pb/dbgtext. Two closures in one function plus one in-function negative control; the population outside dbgtext is UNMEASURED, so treat this as a lever to try, not a census. It says nothing about zeros that are not loop-preheader inits, and nothing about the opposite direction (making two independent `li` become a copy), which is the surviving +0x3cc residual in the same function and is NOT closed by widening scope -- that was probed and folded away.

falsifier: A loop preheader in a function compiled by the same MWCC where converting its counters from function-scope to fresh block-scope locals leaves the object bytes unchanged (NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL) while a li/copy pair is still present, or where the conversion turns two independent `li` INTO a copy. Either observation breaks the direction of the rule. The in-function control also falsifies it: if the mode==3 trailer of fn_800C03E0 (still on function-scope `i`/`k`) ever starts emitting a copy without its source changing, web scope is not the discriminant.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: When a loop preheader must materialise two zeros (a counter and a derived index), MWCC emits either two independent `li rX,0` or one `li` plus an `addi rY,rX,0` copy, and the choice is decided by whether the two variables belong to WEBS THAT SPAN OTHER BLOCKS, not by any spelling of the zero. Give the loop its own block-scope counters and the webs are local, so both zeros are rematerialised independently; leave the loop on function-scope counters that other loops also write and the two zeros share one web, so the second is emitted as a copy. This is source-reachable through DECLARATION SCOPE and through nothing else: the statement POSITION of the initialiser, the initialiser-versus-assignment form, and the operand order of the surrounding expression all fold away before codegen (NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, object bytes unchanged).
